symptoms.symptom: Small amount of water remaining in dispenser (on some models) at end of cycle

causes.label: Normal dispenser operation
remedies: It is normal for a small amount of water to remain in dispenser after the cycle.
To empty water from dispenser drawer, remove drawer and dump water into washer basket or sink.
Empty dispenser prior to putting detergent into dispenser for next cycle.

causes.label: This is normal
remedies: Water may not cover the top level of the clothes.
This is normal for this high efficiency washer.

causes.label: Water valve screens are stopped up
remedies: Turn off the water source and remove the water connection hoses from the upper back of the washer and the house water faucets.
Clean both the hose screens (if so equipped) and the screens in the machine using a brush or a toothpick.
Reconnect the hoses and turn the water back on.
Check to ensure there are no leaks at the connections.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Water valve screens are stopped up"

causes.label: Drain standpipe is too low or hose too far into standpipe
remedies: The drain hose must exceed 30” height at some point between the washer back and the drain pipe.
Use anti-siphon clip.
See the Installation Instructions.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Drain standpipe is too low or hose too far into standpipe"

causes.label: Soft water
remedies: Try less detergent.

causes.label: Too much detergent
remedies: Measure your detergent carefully.
Use less soap if you have soft water, a smaller load or a lightly soiled load.

causes.label: Type of detergent
remedies: Switch to High Efficiency detergent such as      .

causes.label: Type of detergent
remedies: Switch to High Efficiency detergent such as      .

causes.label: Using too much detergent in washer
remedies: Use less detergent.
Use less soap if you have soft water, a smaller load or a lightly soiled load.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Using too much detergent in washer"

causes.label: Fill hoses or drain hose is improperly connected
remedies: Make sure hose connections are tight at faucets and rubber washers are installed.
Make sure end of drain hose is correctly inserted in and secured to drain facility.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Fill hoses or drain hose is improperly connected"

causes.label: Cooler water temperatures provide improved energy efficiency
remedies: New laundry detergents have been formulated to work with cooler water temperatures without affecting wash performance.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Cooler water temperatures provide improved energy efficiency"

causes.label: Water supply is turned off or improperly connected
remedies: Turn both hot and cold faucets fully on and make sure hoses are connected to the correct faucets.
NOTE: Cold water valve inlet is blue.
Hot water valve inlet is red.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 20: "Water supply is turned off or improperly connected"

symptoms.symptom: Washer spins and pauses at the beginning of cycles

causes.label: This is normal
remedies: The washer is sensing the load.

causes.label: The Soak Option was chosen
remedies: This is normal.
The washer alternates between agitate and soak during these cycles to get your clothes cleaner with less wear.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "The Soak Option was chosen"

causes.label: This is normal
remedies: Many cycles incorporate as series of soaks within the agitation period to get your clothes clean with less wear.

symptoms.symptom: Residual powder in dispenser or clogging of dispensers

causes.label: Wash water too cold or low home water pressure
remedies: Select a warmer wash temperature if possible to improve dissolving of detergent or use liquid detergent.
Make sure siphon caps are free of debris and fully pressed into position.
Remove and clean tray if clogging occurs.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Wash water too cold or low home water pressure"

causes.label: Overfilling of dispensers
remedies: Do not overfill or add water to dispenser.
Select Deep Rinse option when using fabric softener.

causes.label: This is normal
remedies: The washer may pause during the spin cycle to remove soapy water more efficiently.

causes.label: Washer is unplugged
remedies: Make sure cord is plugged securely into a working outlet.

causes.label: Water supply is turned off
remedies: Turn both hot and cold faucets fully on.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Water supply is turned off"

causes.label: Lid is open—safety feature prevents agitation and spinning when lid is up
remedies: Close lid and press Start.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Lid is open—safety feature prevents agitation and spinning when lid is up"

causes.label: Circuit breaker/fuse is tripped/blown
remedies: Check house circuit breakers/fuses.
Replace fuses or reset breaker.
Washer should have a separate outlet.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Circuit breaker/fuse is tripped/blown"

causes.label: Electronics need to be reset
remedies: Unplug washer, wait 2 minutes, plug back in and press Start if display is active or press Power if unit is in idle (display blank) mode.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Electronics need to be reset"

causes.label: Start was not pressed
remedies: Press Start.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Start was not pressed"

causes.label: Laundry detergent packet placed in dispenser
remedies: Laundry detergent packets should not be used in the dispensers.
They should only be added directly to the wash basket following the manufacturer’s directions.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Laundry detergent packet placed in dispenser"

causes.label: Changing options
remedies: This is normal.
Several options will change other options to maximize washer performance.

causes.label: Incorrect use of fabric softener
remedies: Check fabric softener package for instructions and follow directions for using dispenser.
Make sure you have selected the Deep Rinse option.
Pretreat stain and rewash using Speed Wash cycle before drying.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Incorrect use of fabric softener"

causes.label: Dye transfer
remedies: Sort whites or lightly colored items from dark colors.

causes.label: Detergent amount
remedies: Be sure to follow detergent manufacturer’s directions.

causes.label: Hard water
remedies: Use a water conditioner or install a water softener.

causes.label: Water is not hot enough
remedies: Make sure water heater is delivering water at 120°F–140°F (48°C– 60°C).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Water is not hot enough"

causes.label: Washer is overloaded
remedies: Loosely load clothes no higher than the top row of holes in the washer basket.
For best results, load items around the outside of the basket.

causes.label: Dye transfer
remedies: Sort clothes by color.
If fabric label states wash separately, unstable dyes may be indicated.

causes.label: Clothes are air or line dried
remedies: If you do not dry your clothes with a clothes dryer, your clothes may retain more lint.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Clothes are air or line dried"

causes.label: Incorrect sorting
remedies: Separate lint producers from lint collectors.

causes.label: Washing too long
remedies: Wash small loads for a shorter time using Light Soil setting.

causes.label: Detergent not dissolving
remedies: Rewash, next time: Try a liquid detergent; Use warmer water temperature.

causes.label: Overloading
remedies: Loosely load clothes in the washer basket.
For best results, load items around the outside of the basket.

causes.label: Incorrect use of fabric softener
remedies: Check fabric softener package for instructions and follow directions for using dispenser.
Make sure you have selected the Deep Rinse option.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 21: "Incorrect use of fabric softener"

symptoms.symptom: Snags, holes, tears, rips or excessive wear

causes.label: Pins, snaps, hooks, sharp buttons, belt buckles, zippers and sharp objects left in pockets
remedies: Fasten snaps, hooks, buttons and zippers.
Remove loose items like pins, objects in pockets and sharp buttons.
Turn knits (which snag easily) inside out.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Pins, snaps, hooks, sharp buttons, belt buckles, zippers and sharp objects left in pockets"

causes.label: Undiluted chlorine bleach
remedies: Check bleach package instructions for proper amount.
Never add undiluted bleach to wash or allow clothes to come in contact with undiluted bleach.

causes.label: Chemicals like hair
remedies: Rinse items that may have chemicals on them before washing.

causes.label: Incorrect wash and dry cycles
remedies: Match Cycle selection to the type of fabric you are washing (especially for easy care loads).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Incorrect wash and dry cycles"

causes.label: Improper sorting
remedies: Avoid mixing heavy items (like jeans) with light items (like blouses).
Try a fabric softener.

causes.label: Overloading
remedies: Loosely load clothes in the washer basket.

causes.label: Repeated washing in water that is too hot
remedies: Wash in warm or cold water.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Repeated washing in water that is too hot"

causes.label: Automatic Temperature Control Valve
remedies: Two valves mix cold and hot water.
The “clicking” is when either valve turns on or off to raise or lower the fill water temperature.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Automatic Temperature Control Valve"

causes.label: Automatic Temperature Control Valve
remedies: Two valves mix cold and hot water.
The “clicking” is when either valve turns on or off to raise or lower the fill water temperature.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Automatic Temperature Control Valve"

causes.label: Motor ramping up/down during spin cycle
remedies: The motor will speed up incrementally during the spin cycle.
When spin is complete, it will coast until it stops.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Motor ramping up/down during spin cycle"

causes.label: Water drain pump
remedies: The drain pump will make a humming sound when pumping out water after agitation stops and continue until spin is complete.

causes.label: Drive motor
remedies: The drive motor will make a “humming” sound during the wash and spin phases of the cycle.

causes.label: Water drain pump
remedies: When the pump starts drawing in air, It starts to gurgle.
The washer should then begin spinning and the sound will continue until it is done spinning.

causes.label: Washing process
remedies: Water swishing while the unit is agitating is normal, especially with smaller loads.

causes.label: Washer leveling legs uneven
remedies: To level the washer, adjust the leveling legs by rotating the individual leg in the proper direction for up or down.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Washer leveling legs uneven"

causes.label: Washer not level and rubbing on cabinet
remedies: To level the washer, adjust the leveling legs by rotating the individual leg in the proper direction for up or down.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 22: "Washer not level and rubbing on cabinet"
